title: Adaptive Quantum Security Bound for TNT
summary: The prior adaptive and tight-security proofs for TNT are flawed; a valid quantum security bound, potentially degraded, remains to be established.

formal_statement.body: Determine the strongest valid adaptive quantum security bound for TNT, possibly weaker than the previously claimed tight bound.

scope.domain: Adaptive quantum security analysis of the TNT symmetric construction.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine the strongest valid adaptive quantum security bound for TNT, including whether the previously claimed tight bound can be recovered or only a weaker bound can be proved.

citations.label: Mind the Bad Norms: Revisiting Compressed Oracle-based Quantum Indistinguishability Proofs

progress.summary: The paper finds flaws in the prior adaptive and tight-security proofs for TNT. It suggests that defining bad events through database entries may support a proof with a worse bound, but leaves that proof open.
citation_labels: Ritam Bhaumik et al., Mind the Bad Norms: Revisiting Compressed Oracle-based Quantum Indistinguishability Proofs
